market_context: Risk-off conditions dominate after core PCE rose 3.3% year over year versus 3.2% expected, reinforcing rate-hike bets, while the administration proposed additional 20% tariffs on major trading partners (finance.yahoo.com). Stocks have rebounded sharply from their opening lows by 10:00 ET, but the AI and semiconductor rout, VIX at 34.70, and reduced exposure appetite before the Thanksgiving closure leave that bounce vulnerable (cnbc.com).

predictions.reasoning: SPY has rebounded from $695.45 to approximately its $703.38 premarket print, a logical resistance area after the gap lower ([chartexchange.com). With hot inflation and tariff concerns still pressuring valuations, I expect a partial retracement of the opening bounce rather than a sustained recovery.

QQQ's recovery from $607.76 has returned it to roughly the $617.14 premarket level recorded at 9:06 a.m., while technology remains the center of the selloff (stocktitan.net). Premarket losses were led by Nvidia, Micron, AMD and Marvell, making another fade in the tech-heavy fund the more likely outcome (finance.yahoo.com).

Nvidia fell 6.3% premarket and nearly 9% shortly after the open; its current rebound only brings it back to the approximately $145.70 premarket area rather than reversing the chip selloff (finance.yahoo.com, cnbc.com). Continued concerns about AI profitability should pressure shares back toward today's $141.17 low.

META shows substantial relative strength, down only 0.76% versus QQQ's 3.20% decline and trading near its $586.49 session high after recovering from $567.75. It was also the least weak of the major hyperscalers cited premarket at a 2.3% decline, supporting a modest further grind higher if buyers continue rotating into the session's stronger names (finance.yahoo.com).
